status: OPEN FOR MERGE, planner-owned. PR 38 opened, NOT merged, NOT deployed. Both items delivered. Both mechanisms established by measurement, and the second one turned out to rest on a false premise that was worth more than the fix.
missionPremise: Two defects G-99 measured and routed rather than took, because web/ was named untouchable in its dispatch and two lanes were live in it (`_inbox/2026-08-20_k2_close.json`, whatRemainsOpen). FIRST: `.prov .sep` paints a `|` at 1.856:1 light and 1.737:1 dark against a 4.5:1 requirement, on every surface, and axe reports it in NO bucket at all - not violations, not passes, not incomplete - because axe-core excludes punctuation-only text from color-contrast by design (axe.js:28714, `removeUnicodeOptions = { punctuations: true }` feeding hasRealTextChildren). That is worse than a ceiling set too low: no ceiling, no adjudication and no environment would ever have caught it, which is why G-99 built a second instrument rather than tuning the first. SECOND, and G-99 flagged it against itself: `axe surfaces 5 .p-ok nodes on Windows and 0 on Linux while coverage reads 100% on both` - and a coverage figure that says 100% while two environments disagree about what is in it is measuring something other than what a reader will think it measures. It lands in an Accessibility Conformance Report, which is a legal document, so a figure whose bound is not stated beside it is the DEV_PROCESS 1.2 defect where it costs the most.
completionPredicate: An auditor reads the gate's number and cannot mistake CONTAINMENT for JUDGEMENT: the figure that leads is what axe actually evaluated, the containment figure stands beside it with its own word, and both carry their counting rule at the point of use. The separator is either compliant or genuinely out of the accessibility tree, proven with an instrument that is not axe - because axe never saw it and aria-hidden does not silence axe anyway - and its 1.856:1 does not vanish from the record when it becomes exempt. Rendered text that no instrument judged and no exemption covers has a name, a number and a build refusal with a plant behind it. The Windows/Linux disagreement is explained or explicitly still open with what was ruled out. Every G-99 property still holds, each one exercised rather than asserted. The CI check-run conclusion string on the head SHA is the authority and the branch is open for a planner merge rather than merged. All of that is met and evidenced below with raw output; what is NOT met is in whatRemainsOpen rather than narrated away.
scopeBasis: Six files. web/index.html is the product edit and it is one attribute repeated twenty times; the other five are the gate and its wiring, which this lane owns outright because nothing else is running in this repo. web/sc-kit.css is UNTOUCHED and byte-identical to main - proven by normalising line endings on both sides to defeat the autocrlf artifact: `tr -d '\r' < web/sc-kit.css | md5sum` = ac6cb7458a66583cefaf62f5584490c7 and `git show main:web/sc-kit.css | tr -d '\r' | md5sum` = the same, with `git diff main --numstat -- web/sc-kit.css` printing no row at all. That matters more than usual: the kit is byte-identical across three repos, its own header says a repo that edits a token value has forked the system, and G-102 is live in the kit's copy in P:/tmp/l2-kit. web/shell.css is untouched too, and that is a DECISION rather than an omission: the .sep colour is NOT repainted. The fix is the declared-decorative route, and raising --sc-line-strong would be repainting a hairline token that three repos consume, which is a kit-shaped call this lane has no standing to make. Also deliberately out: web/app.js, src/a11y-surfaces.mjs (still needs no change - the surface list was already derived and the new axes belong to the scanner, which is the same conclusion G-99 reached), live Bastrop, G-52, G-24, L26, and every other lane's clone.

theDECORATIVELEDGER_aTwoWayContract.why: aria-hidden="true" is the strongest instrument-silencing attribute in this product: it removes text from the accessibility tree, from 1.4.3's scope and from the second instrument's computed population in ONE attribute. Left undeclared, using it is indistinguishable from fixing the defect, and the 1.856:1 that made the exemption necessary leaves the record entirely.
soItRefusesBOTHDIRECTIONS: an aria-hidden text element matching NO entry fails the build (undeclared-decorative), matched with the DOM's own matches()/closest() rather than a string heuristic on a computed selector
an entry matching NOTHING across the whole run fails the build (exemption-outlived-its-cause), on the same terms a waiver's zero arm does
and the ratio is recomputed and printed every run even though the element is exempt, so the conformance report states the exemption WITH its measurement
theDECORATIVELEDGER_aTwoWayContract.andTheEntryCarriesAFieldAWaiverDoesNot: andWhatThisDoesNOTClaim - asserted by the test on every entry - because the whole risk of a decorative exemption is that it reads as 'the defect is fixed' when it means 'the text is out of scope', and the entry is the only place that distinction can sit next to the number.

plantFiringPROOFS_fullGateRunsNotUnitTes.whyTheTHIRDONEMatters: punctuation-contrast is G-99's plant and it had a waiver behind it. With the real .sep now declared decorative and that waiver deleted, the plant must still fire on its own - it plants a p.sep that is NOT aria-hidden, so the sweep computes it, and with an empty ledger there is nothing to absorb it.
